renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: insert_length_profile
  title: Insert length distribution
  description: |-
    Each curve is a sample: the share of its full-length non-chimeric reads in each 100 bp bin of insert length. It answers what transcript sizes the library captured.
    How to read: a broad curve with a main peak at the expected transcript size is a healthy library. A curve piled at short lengths points to degraded RNA or fragmentation, and a hard cut on the right to a size selection. Compare the samples: curves that differ in shape were not prepared the same way.
    Note: isoseq refine publishes no cut-off for the insert length.
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Insert length (bp)
    y_title: Share of FLNC reads per 100 bp (%)
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: length_bp
    y: pct

- component: figure
  title: Insert length by sample
  description: |-
    Each line is a sample: the share of its full-length non-chimeric reads per length bin. It answers whether the samples share the same size profile.
    How to read: overlapping lines mean consistent library preparation. A line shifted to the left holds shorter inserts, which is the first thing to check when a sample has few long isoforms.
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: length_bp
    y: pct
    color: sample
    labels:
      length_bp: Insert length (bp)
      pct: Share of FLNC reads (%)
      sample: Sample

- component: table
  title: Insert length bins
  description: |-
    Each row is a length bin of one sample: the read count, its share of the sample and the cumulative share up to that length. It answers where a given fraction of the reads falls.
    How to read: the cumulative column gives the length below which a given share of the reads lies, for instance the median insert.

- component: card
  title: Full-length non-chimeric reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of full-length non-chimeric (FLNC) reads, the reads that carry both primers and a poly(A) tail without being a concatemer, with the median and the largest library next to it. It answers how much usable transcript data the run produced.
    How to read: a large gap between the median and the maximum means uneven libraries. Open the bar chart to see which ones are small.
    Source: https://isoseq.how/getting-started.html
  column: flnc_reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: per library, the median and the largest
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Non-chimeric share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of full-length reads that survive chimera removal, with the spread across libraries in the box. It answers how clean the libraries are.
    How to read: a high share with a tight box means little concatemer contamination. A library far below the others had many artificial concatemers, so check its preparation. isoseq refine publishes no cut-off for this share.
  column: pct_flnc
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with the spread

- component: card
  title: Poly(A) share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of FLNC reads that still carry a poly(A) tail, with the spread across libraries in the box. It answers how many reads kept the tail the refine step looks for.
    How to read: the share depends on the library preparation, so compare libraries made the same way. A library far from its peers had a different poly(A) capture. isoseq refine publishes no cut-off for this share.
  column: pct_polya
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with the spread

- component: figure
  title: Full-length non-chimeric reads per library
  description: |-
    Each bar is a library: its count of full-length non-chimeric reads, coloured by the sample it belongs to. It answers which libraries contribute most to a sample.
    How to read: a sample made of several libraries of very different size depends on its largest one. A very short bar is a library worth checking for a failed run.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median FLNC read count of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Iso-Seq.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: library
    y: flnc_reads
    color: sample
    labels:
      library: Library
      flnc_reads: FLNC reads
      sample: Sample
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: flnc_reads

- component: table
  title: Refine summary per library
  description: |-
    Each row is a library: its full-length, non-chimeric and poly(A) read counts and the two shares. It answers which libraries lost the most reads to chimera removal.
    How to read: sort by the non-chimeric share to find libraries with many concatemers.
